Before You Flip: Which Renovations Actually Increase Property Value?

Fresh paint and a beautiful kitchen can transform a house—but a successful flip is about the numbers behind the reveal.

By Reddy Appraisal LLCOctober 22, 20262 min read

IN THIS ARTICLE

Keep the local buyer in mindWork backward from supportable valueLeave room for surprisesMore in Home Improvements ↗← All 24 articles

THE SHORT ANSWER

An attractive flip still needs room for surprises and a realistic resale timeline. If your projected profit disappears after a modest cost overrun or price reduction, reconsider the deal.

Keep the local buyer in mind

Fresh paint and a beautiful kitchen can transform a house—but a successful flip is about the numbers behind the reveal. Investors sometimes spend heavily on finishes without considering what buyers in that specific neighborhood are willing to pay. In Tucson, a renovation that makes sense in one price range may be difficult to recover in another.

Work backward from supportable value

Work backward from a supportable after-repair value (ARV). Study recent renovated sales that match the home's size, location, and overall quality, then build a budget that includes purchase costs, permits, labor, carrying costs, selling expenses, and a contingency. Prioritize repairs that address safety, functionality, and obvious condition issues before paying for luxury upgrades that nearby sales don't support.

Leave room for surprises

An attractive flip still needs room for surprises and a realistic resale timeline. If your projected profit disappears after a modest cost overrun or price reduction, reconsider the deal. A residential appraisal informed by relevant comparable sales can provide another perspective on current or proposed-improvement value, subject to the assignment's scope, before you commit.
